summary: Tested Microsoft sign-in, Support Worker password auth, user types, the Microsoft integrations and Socials, on both backend and frontend. Backend: 25 of 26 pytest checks pass. The one failure is a security issue: the user's bcrypt password_hash comes back in /auth/login, /auth/me, /auth/change-password and /auth/session responses. Frontend: the app CRASHED ON LOAD for every user. The error boundary showed 'Screen names must be unique: change-password' because _layout.tsx registered the change-password Stack.Screen in two Stack.Protected groups. Testing agent applied a minimal fix to unblock testing. After the fix, every requested UI flow passed: Microsoft button shows the not-set-up error, Support Worker password login, admin adds a worker and sees the temp password dialog, the forced change-password screen blocks the app, Change type sheet, Reset password, Remove, Socials (3 websites, Instagram and Facebook only), Integrations (SharePoint, Outlook, Teams, with non-Teams URLs rejected), and regression screens. No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch) were found.

critical.issue: The user object includes password_hash (bcrypt), plus failed_logins and locked_until. Cause: core.user_from_token and auth.py return db.users.find_one(..., P), and P only excludes _id. The hash is then saved in client state. Fix: use a projection that excludes password_hash, failed_logins and locked_until (e.g. USER_P = {'_id':0,'password_hash':0,'failed_logins':0,'locked_until':0}) in user_from_token and in every user returned from auth.py. change_password already reads the hash separately.

minor.issue: LinkedIn code is still present: SOCIAL_LABELS, status.linkedin, /integrations/linkedin/start and /integrations/linkedin/callback, and redirect_uris.linkedin. The user asked for LinkedIn to be removed. No UI shows it.

Changing a support_worker to an office type removes password_hash but keeps their existing sessions. The user stays signed in with password-based sessions after becoming a Microsoft-only type. Consider deleting their sessions.

Anyone who knows a worker's email can lock that account with 5 bad attempts (intended lockout, but there is no per-IP limit). An office user with no password who gets 5 bad attempts is also given failed_logins and locked_until, which serves no purpose.
No 'general' channel in conversations (only Allied Health, announcements, Celebrate the Wins). Check whether the seed by seed_key/name ran after the migration.

ui_bugs.issue: CRASH (fixed by testing agent): Stack.Screen 'change-password' was declared twice, once in the must_change_password guard and once in the signed-in guard. React Navigation threw 'Screen names must be unique', and the whole app showed the ErrorBoundary for all users, including on the login screen. Fix: one change-password screen in a Stack.Protected guard={!!user} block placed after the main (tabs) block, with headerShown false when must_change_password is true. change-password.tsx now calls router.replace('/') after a successful forced change.

The temp-password Modal opens in the same tick as the add sheet or ConfirmSheet Modal closes. On iOS native, a second RN Modal presented while another is dismissing often fails to appear, and the password is 'shown only once'. Open the dialog after the first modal's onDismiss, or use a single modal. The temp password also has no Copy button (expo-clipboard).

issues: It still shows the old role pill 'Admin/Employee' plus the group 'Support Workers'. It should show the new user type (Executive / Admin / Support Office / Support Worker).
Line 78 still has the emerging_therapist PathwaySummary branch. That group no longer exists, so this is dead code.
The Outlook calendar card has no status line when not configured. Only the SharePoint card says 'Waiting for the Microsoft 365 app details'.
The logo-google icon is still used for attached SharePoint files and for the certificate drive_link indicator.
After a successful change, the user stays on the screen with only a toast. Consider router.back().

Update /app/memory/test_credentials.md. It still says 'Emergent-managed Google Sign-In (no passwords)' and that emp is emerging_therapist. Add the emp.test@example.com / TestWorker#2026 password login and the Microsoft notes.
critical_code_review_comments: Cause of the leak: P={'_id':0} is used for user lookups that are returned to clients. Only the users.py list and add_user responses exclude password_hash.
Lockout compares ISO strings (locked_until > now_iso()). This works because both are UTC isoformat, but it is fragile. Prefer datetime values.

NEW_STARTER_GROUPS (new_starter_employee/contractor) no longer match any staff_group after the migration (only support_worker/support_office). The Library 'New Starter checklist' row and the starter-related profile logic can never trigger.
auth_session: a login code is single-use (find_one_and_delete), and expiry is checked correctly.

Microsoft start/callback: state, PKCE, nonce and tenant checks look correct. Unknown Microsoft users and Support Worker types are rejected. Not exercised end to end because MS credentials are not set.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested flows after the testing agent's crash fix (0% before: app crashed on load)

Changing emp.test's password via the API deletes the test_session_employee session, so re-insert it afterwards. Teams-link testIDs use the channel name with spaces, e.g. 'teams-link-Allied Health'.
rca_of_issue: App crash: expo-router Stack.Protected removes routes whose guard is false, but React Navigation still validates the full set of declared names. Declaring 'change-password' in two Protected groups makes the name duplicate. Reproduce: load any URL and the ErrorBoundary shows 'Screen names must be unique'. Mitigation: declare it once with a guard of !!user, after the (tabs) group, so normal users still land on (tabs) and forced users can only reach change-password.
